slot.archetype: volume from density then PV = nRT
slot.brief: From gas density at given T and P, compute molar mass or volume via the ideal gas equation.

stem: An ideal gas has a density of $2.0\ \text{g L}^{-1}$ at $1.23\ \text{atm}$ and $300\ \text{K}$. Its molar mass is (take $R = 0.082\ \text{L atm K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$):
working:
$\rho = \dfrac{PM}{RT} \Rightarrow M = \dfrac{\rho RT}{P}$
$M = \dfrac{(2.0)(0.082)(300)}{1.23} = 40\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$

Independent check: Using \(M=\frac{dRT}{P}=\frac{(2.0)(0.082)(300)}{1.23}=40\ \text{g mol}^{-1}\).
